signature.name: Clifton Suspension Bridge
signature.detail: Bristol's most famous sight, a graceful Victorian span over the Avon Gorge with sweeping views. Walk across for free at any time; early morning or sunset gives the best light and fewer crowds.

signature.name: SS Great Britain
signature.detail: Brunel's pioneering iron steamship, now a museum where you can go below the glass 'waterline' into the restored hull. Book tickets online in advance and allow a couple of hours; it sits in the harbour, a short walk from the city centre.

signature.name: Bristol Harbour
signature.detail: The lively heart of the city, ringed by boats, markets and waterfront walks. Wander the harbourside in the afternoon and stay for dinner; it is an easy walk from Bristol Temple Meads station.

signature.name: M Shed
signature.detail: A free museum on the harbourside telling Bristol's story through local voices and exhibits. Entry is free, so it is a good rainy-day stop; check opening days before you go.

signature.name: Bristol Museum & Art Gallery
signature.detail: A free museum with natural history, art and archaeology, close to the university and Brandon Hill. Combine it with a climb up Cabot Tower nearby; admission is free but donations are welcome.

signature.name: Bristol Cathedral
signature.detail: A striking medieval cathedral with a fine vaulted interior, near the harbourside. Entry is generally free; visit on a weekday morning for quiet and check service times before you go.

signature.name: Brandon Hill
signature.detail: A green hill in the city centre topped by Cabot Tower, with free views over Bristol. Climb the tower on a clear day; it is a short walk from Park Street and the museum.

signature.name: We The Curious
signature.detail: An interactive science centre on the harbourside, great for families and curious adults. Book tickets online and allow half a day; it is a short walk from M Shed.

transport: Bus single around $2.50-3; day tickets good value
